note: Regions for tools/build_pilot_manifest.py. Each region names a gap survey site as its anchor, a box to search for small water bodies, and a terrain setting. The settings are descriptions, not measurements. Customer water bodies never enter this repository (assumption A8).

regions.name: Lake Tahoe basin, California and Nevada
regions.setting_basis: Sierra Nevada basin. The lake surface is near 1,900 m with steep relief on every shore.
regions.why: Mountain terrain with snow and shadow. The anchor lake straddles UTM zones 10 and 11, so it lies in two tiles.

regions.name: Lake Lanier area, Georgia
regions.setting_basis: Piedmont with rolling hills. The lake surface is near 330 m.
regions.why: Dendritic reservoir shown in the Discovery maps, with many farm and golf ponds nearby.

regions.name: Lake Okeechobee north shore, Florida
regions.setting_basis: Florida lowland. The lake surface is near 5 m and the surrounding land is nearly level.
regions.why: Subtropical flat terrain with many small ponds and a bloom-prone anchor lake.

regions.name: Grand Lake St. Marys area, Ohio
regions.setting_basis: Ohio till plain under farmland. The lake surface is near 265 m.
regions.why: Flat farmland with a shallow bloom-prone reservoir and small ponds.

regions.name: Lake Washington area, Washington
regions.setting_basis: Seattle area with low relief and built-up shores.
regions.why: Urban ponds beside an urban lake.

regions.name: Iliamna Lake north-east shore, Alaska
regions.setting_basis: Alaska Peninsula with low mountains and tundra at high latitude.
regions.why: High latitude with low winter sun. The anchor lake is too large to carry, so only small lakes are included.
